title: enterprise-weighted-intake-heuristics-for-hosted-multi-feature-requests
creator: Marcus Li
summary: Create a repeatable, signal-rich intake rubric that ranks hosted API feature requests involving chat, streaming, tool/function-calls, or structured outputs by enterprise risk, SLO impact, and revenue enablement.
description: Customers regularly submit compound feature requests (chat + streaming + tool calls + structured output) that blur existing prioritization paths. This ticket defines a weighted, explainable intake heuristic and an operational triage playbook capturing signals, thresholds, and routing rules to accelerate decision-making for Hosted API feature requests and ensure predictable enterprise onboarding and SLA decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake rubric with numeric weights for: customer SLA needs, data residency/KMS constraints, request complexity (multi-step tool-calls), streaming latency sensitivity, structured output correctness requirements, and revenue/ARR potential.

An internal triage checklist and playbook that maps score ranges to routing actions: auto-approve backlog, schedule PM/SE discovery, escalate to enterprise intake council, or initiate security/architecture review.
A lightweight prototype form in the intake tooling (Confluence + Intake spreadsheet) demonstrating how signals are captured for 5 representative enterprise requests.
A documented handoff flow and list of owners for decisions requiring Dedicated or Private deployment considerations.
Stakeholder sign-off from Solutions Engineering, Security, and a pilot customer for at least one representative request.
A post-triage dashboard query that shows time-to-decision and triage outcomes for the next 30 days.
Security review checklist completed for scenarios where customer data must remain within VPC or requires HSM/KMS integration.
decision_log: 2025-01-28: Kickoff with PM, SE, and Security to align on problem statement and examples of compound requests.
2025-01-30: Agreed to use a weighted scoring model instead of binary buckets to reduce edge-case churn.
2025-02-02: Decided weights: SLA sensitivity (25%), Data locality/security (20%), Technical complexity (20%), Streaming latency (15%), Revenue/ARR (10%), Integration risk (10%).
2025-02-04: Identified requirement for security_review_required flag when data residency or KMS/HSM is involved; assigned Security owner.
2025-02-04: Determined that high-weighted requests (score >= 80) route to Enterprise Intake Council for accelerated timeline and dedicated capacity evaluation.
next_steps: Finalize numeric weights and publish rubric on Confluence for internal review by 2025-02-07.
SE to collect 10 recent enterprise requests and score them against the rubric to validate distribution by 2025-02-10.
Implement a simple intake form (Google Forms prototype) that emits computed score and triage recommendation by 2025-02-11.
Schedule triage runbook review with Security and Solutions Engineering on 2025-02-12.
Pilot the rubric on three live customer requests and collect feedback; iterate weights before embedding in intake tooling.
notes: Design implication: intake form must capture structured output schema requirements and acceptance tests to estimate QA burden.
Operational note: requests that include external tool integrations (webhooks/external API keys) should add an additional integration-security review step.
Edge case: legacy customers insisting on on-prem bundle should trigger Private deployment review even if initial score is moderate.
Run-rate assumption: ~5 compound enterprise intake items per quarter for pilot customers; rubric must avoid excessive false positives to prevent council fatigue.
